done.why: A wizard cast a fence in the Dark Tunnel. Every exit but the way I came was blocked, and the way back (northeast) was blocked too. I could not find any way out.

about: An underground cave adventure that feels like Zork. You start in a barrow with a lamp and a sword. You cross a bridge, pass through a great cavern, and enter a dark tunnel where a wizard shows up.

moments.note: 'Cross the bridge south' said 'You can't see any such thing.' The world seems to want plain direction words.
Going south put me in pitch black with a grue warning.
A wizard appeared and cast a Fence spell.
Southeast, southwest and northeast were all blocked, and nothing hinted at how to get out.
'Examine the fence' wasn't understood, so I could not look closer at the obstacle.
Waiting, saying 'fence' and waving the sword all did nothing. I was stuck.

wished: Examine or look at the fence and the wizard.
Retreat the way I came, since the fence also blocked the way back.
Some hint about what the fence wants from me.

lines.line: The Wizard, in a deep and resonant voice, speaks the word "Fence!" He then vanishes, cackling gleefully.
lines.why: This is the moment I got trapped, and it is also the most vivid line.

lines.line: It is pitch black. You are likely to be eaten by a grue.
lines.why: A tense warning that did what it was meant to.

fun.why: The opening was pleasant, but I got trapped within about 20 turns.

engagement.why: The cavern and the wizard's arrival drew me in, until the dead end.

difficulty.why: With every exit blocked and nothing to try, I could not make any progress.

interestingness.why: The cave setting and the wizard are promising, but I saw little of them.

prose.why: The descriptions were atmospheric and clear.
